newsitem.title: JAPAN: Peugeot aims to sell 20,000 cars in Japan in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot aims to sell 20,000 cars in Japan in 2000.

text.p: Inchcape Peugeot Japan Co Ltd, the Japanese import and distribution unit for Peugeot cars, said on Tuesday it aims at Japanese sales of 20,000 cars in the year 2000.
"We hope to boost our Japanese sales to 20,000 units in 2000 by introducing new models and increasing sales outlets," a Peugeot Japan spokesman said.
Peugeot Japan hopes to achieve sales of 6,000 or 7,000 cars in calendar 1997 by launching new models later this year, the spokesman said.
The company plans to increase its Japanese sales outlets to 100 points by the year 2000 from the present 80.

Japanese sales of Peugeot cars in January-June period rose a steep 26.4 percent from a year earlier to 2,502 units, mainly helped by good demand for the Peugeot 306 model, while overall Japanese sales of imported cars fell 9.3 percent in the same period, according to industry data.
Inchcape Peugeot Japan is owned fifty-fifty by Inchcape Overseas Ltd, a unit of Inchcape Plc, and Automobiles Peugeot, a unit of PSA Peugeot Citroen.
